note: 'the teacher checking the booking' loses its subject: 'the teacher' stands as a conjunct of a coordination with 'flow chart' instead of the subject of 'checking'
'round to Scan again' is no command: 'round' is written as the verb of an imperative clause, though the words describe 'arrow out of Scan and round to Scan again'
'Start' is written as the verb of an imperative clause in 'a line from Start to Approve', though 'Start' names one end of the line
'like' is held in `discourse`, though the words say 'remove it like before'
sop:
@c1 syntax.clause form=imperative verb="remove" modifier="like" modifier="before" complement=$n1
@n1 syntax.nominal head="it"

note: 'like' is the head of a nominal in 'exactly like before the last swap', though it is a linking word and no thing is named by it
'this time includes more details' is tied to nothing, though it says what the second 'try again' gives
'bring it back up on the screen and give it a proper size' are commands written as `declarative` clauses, so the request is stated instead of asked
